heroBody: The iPhone 16 is the mainstream Apple phone in 2026 — the A18 chip, the Camera Control button, the brighter OLED panel, and the USB‑C port that finally replaces Lightning across the lineup. US pricing has settled into a pattern: Apple holds the list price, Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart and Target undercut on promotions, and the carrier‑locked versions (with bill credits) trade the headline 'free' price for a long‑term commitment. This page pulls live US listings from BuyWhere's catalog every few minutes so you can see the current floor for the unlocked 128GB, which retailer is undercutting, and where the carrier‑with‑bill‑credit version actually pencils out cheaper for someone who would have switched to that carrier anyway.

highlights.title: Camera Control and the A18
highlights.body: The iPhone 16 introduced the Camera Control capacitive button and the A18 chip, which is meaningfully faster than the A16 in the iPhone 15 and unlocks Apple Intelligence on‑device. If you shoot a lot of photos or use generative photo tools, this is the single biggest jump over an iPhone 14 or 15.

highlights.title: USB‑C, finally standard across the lineup
highlights.body: Every iPhone 16 ships with USB‑C and supports the same charging cable as iPad and MacBook. If you have been holding on to an iPhone with Lightning purely for cable convenience, that argument is gone.

highlights.title: Storage and the 128GB trap
highlights.body: Apple still ships a 128GB tier on the base iPhone 16, and in 2026 that is uncomfortably tight for anyone shooting ProRAW video or carrying offline music libraries. The 256GB tier is the smarter floor for most buyers; the live prices on this page show the gap.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pay the least without getting burned
advicePoints: Time it: Apple rarely discounts the iPhone 16 outside Black Friday and a spring promo. Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart undercut more often and earlier — set a price alert on this page rather than waiting for a single day.

Trade‑in stacks: an iPhone 13 or newer in good condition is worth a meaningful Apple trade‑in credit and an even larger credit at the carriers when bundled with a new line. The headline 'free iPhone' is real only if you would have switched to that carrier and ported a number anyway.

Prefer unlocked if you travel or switch carriers: the unlocked iPhone 16 from Apple, Amazon or Best Buy is the right default. Carrier‑locked SKUs are cheaper at checkout but bill you back over 24–36 months.

Avoid unknown sellers on marketplaces: listings well below the floor from unknown sellers are usually refurbished units sold as new or international variants without US warranty. Stick to Amazon‑sold, Apple‑sold, or the big three electronics chains.
Buy AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss only if you have a real history of dropping phones — the base AppleCare+ covers the same screen and battery failure for less.
faqSectionTitle: iPhone 16 in the US — common questions

faqs.question: Is the iPhone 16 worth it over the iPhone 15 in the US?
faqs.answer: Yes for most buyers — the Camera Control button, A18 chip and USB‑C are real daily‑use upgrades over the iPhone 15. If you have an iPhone 14 or older the jump is large; from an iPhone 15 it is incremental.

faqs.question: Is the iPhone 16 worth it over the iPhone 16 Pro?
faqs.answer: For most shoppers the base iPhone 16 is enough. The Pro adds the telephoto camera, ProMotion and a brighter display. Only power users who shoot telephoto regularly or want the larger Pro Max battery should pay the Pro premium.

faqs.question: When is the iPhone 16 cheapest in the US?
faqs.answer: Historically during Black Friday week and a spring promo in March/April. Carrier bill‑credit deals run year‑round but lock you in for 24–36 months. The live prices on this page show the current floor.

faqs.question: Which iPhone 16 storage tier should I buy?
faqs.answer: 256GB is the smart floor in 2026 unless you rely entirely on iCloud. 128GB is fine if you shoot mostly in Standard HEIF and stream your music library; 512GB matters only if you shoot a lot of 4K video on the device.
